as_told.title: How the UAP Task Force was set up to hunt down legacy programs

plain: Starting around 2019 and 2020, efforts to get at the government's UFO secrets picked up speed, with the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study unexplained objects (UAP is the government's term for UFOs), doing its work under orders from Congress. The national security analyst Matthew Pines tells it this way. He says Congress heard things after the news stories of 2017 and 2018, along with private back-channel conversations, and decided a formal group was needed to dig in, including into hidden older programs. Pines also points to the yearly defense spending law, the National Defense Authorization Act, and to the work of an intelligence officer named David Grusch and a retired Army colonel named Karl Nell.
